bug: [GC] WasmEdge segfault on `ref.cast eqref` after `table.get`
### Summary

# WasmEdge SIGSEGV: `ref.cast` on null reference from concrete-typed table

## Version

- WasmEdge 0.16.1, commit `3ad922d67525975f6b4ec0e382604d91f97354bd`
- Linux 5.15.0-168-generic x86\_64

## Minimal Reproducer

```wat
(module
  (type $s (struct))
  (table 1 (ref null $s))
  (func (export "run")
    i32.const 0
    table.get 0      ;; null (ref null $s) from uninitialized slot
    ref.cast eqref   ;; CRASH
    drop
  )
)
```

```bash
wasm-tools parse crash.wat -o crash.wasm
wasm-tools validate crash.wasm   # OK
wasmedge crash.wasm run          # Segmentation fault
d8 run.js -- crash.wasm                 # OK
```

## GDB Analysis

```bash
gdb -batch -ex "run" -ex "bt" -ex "x/5i \$rip-4" -ex "info registers rax r15" \
  -ex "x/2gx \$r15" --args /users/khan22/.wasmedge/bin/wasmedge crash.wasm run
```

```
Thread 2 "wasmedge" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007ffff1c6ca05 in ?? () from /users/khan22/.wasmedge/lib/libwasmedge.so.0.1.0

#0  0x00007ffff1c6ca05  libwasmedge.so.0
#1  0x00007ffff1c6d25c  libwasmedge.so.0

#9  0x00007ffff0eeaac3  start_thread (pthread_create.c:442)

   0x7ffff1c6ca01:  mov    0x8(%r15),%rax    ; load object pointer
=> 0x7ffff1c6ca05:  mov    (%rax),%rax        ; CRASH: rax = 0x0
   0x7ffff1c6ca08:  mov    %rdi,%rcx
   0x7ffff1c6ca0b:  mov    %rsi,%r8
   0x7ffff1c6ca0e:  test   %rax,%rax          ; null check (too late)
   0x7ffff1c6ca11:  je     0x7ffff1c6ca28

rax  0x0
r15  0x7fffec000cd0

0x7fffec000cd0:  0x0000000800630000   0x0000000000000000
                 (type: struct idx 8)  (object pointer: NULL)
```

Corresponding location in `/users/khan22/.wasmedge/lib/libwasmedge.so.0.1.0` (text base `0x7ffff141c000`):

```bash
objdump -d --start-address=0x8509a0 --stop-address=0x850a30 \
  /users/khan22/.wasmedge/lib/libwasmedge.so.0.1.0
```

```asm
850a01:  49 8b 47 08          mov    0x8(%r15),%rax
850a05:  48 8b 00             mov    (%rax),%rax       ; NULL deref
850a0e:  48 85 c0             test   %rax,%rax         ; null check after deref maybe?
850a11:  74 15                je     850a28
```

## (Potential) Root Cause

`table.get` on a concrete-typed table (`(table N (ref null $type))`) returns a null reference with object pointer `0x0` on the interpreter value stack. The `ref.cast` handler then dereferences this pointer to read the type descriptor before checking for null. The null check exists but is placed after the dereference.

## Acknowledgement
This bug has been found during development process of `GCsmith`.

content.text:
I fixed the crash by adding a null check before the dereference, but I haven't built it or run any tests, including your reproducer.

When `table.get` reads an empty slot from a table like `(ref null $s)`, it returns a null reference that still carries the concrete type `$s`. The code in the cast and test paths assumed null references only ever carry an abstract type. It therefore dereferenced the object pointer without checking it, which is the null read in your GDB trace.

The check is now `if (Inst && Inst->getModule())` in three places:
- **`runRefTestOp`** in `lib/executor/engine/refInstr.cpp` (interpreter, `ref.test` and `ref.cast`).
- **`proxyRefTest`** in `lib/executor/engine/proxy.cpp` (compiled code, `ref.test`).
- **`proxyRefCast`** in `lib/executor/engine/proxy.cpp` (compiled code, `ref.cast`).

When the pointer is null, the type check falls back to the current module's type list. That works for your reproducer because `$s` is defined in the same module. I didn't check a null reference whose concrete type comes from another module. In that case the type indices could be looked up in the wrong list.

For your example, `ref.cast eqref` on that null should now succeed instead of crashing. I also replaced the old comment claiming null references never carry a concrete type, since your case shows it's wrong.
